verdict.strongest_covered_cluster: The central review lifecycle is strongest: pull-request intake resolution, context budgeting, review-unit partitioning, concurrent specialist dispatch, aggregation/deduplication/severity reconciliation, confidence and head filtering, high-severity source verification, policy-driven publication, and human calibration are all visibly connected.
verdict.most_consequential_gap: The intake safety gate is incomplete: the board omits both rejection of draft pull requests and exclusion of vendored/generated paths before model work. It also omits the reviewer call-budget exhaustion behavior.
verdict.coverage_summary: Weighted coverage is 44.5 of 63, or 0.7063. The main architecture and its publication, calibration, head-change, and daily-budget loops are substantially represented. However, multiple system-defining operational semantics are absent, especially draft rejection, pre-model path exclusion, and graceful handling of exhausted reviewer tool budgets; several detailed contracts are only partial, including context contents, finding fields, stale-location dropping, unverified non-publication, restart against the new head, and telemetry dimensions. The base rubric score is 5 because coverage is at least 0.60 but below 0.72; the absent-system-defining cap of 6 does not further reduce it.
